entries.title: Comment periods close November 23, 2026 on both OCC GENIUS Act payment stablecoin information collections
entries.facts: The Federal Register records two Office of the Comptroller of the Currency notices published on October 23, 2026 whose comment periods close on November 23, 2026. Document 2026-21704, Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Information Collection; Submission for OMB Review; Applications for Licensing or Registration To Issue Payment Stablecoins Under the GENIUS Act, appears at 91 FR 66939 to 66942. Document 2026-21705, covering reporting forms and instructions for permitted payment stablecoin issuers subject to the jurisdiction of the OCC, appears at 91 FR 66916 to 66939. Each carries the action line Notice and request for comment and the dates line Comments must be received by November 23, 2026. Both notices accompany the OCC payment stablecoin final rule, Federal Register document 2026-21706 at 91 FR 67000, RIN 1557-AF41, docket OCC-2025-0372, which is effective January 18, 2027.
entries.source_label: Federal Register documents 2026-21704 and 2026-21705, OCC, published October 23, 2026; records retrieved from the Federal Register documents API at federalregister.gov
entries.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers, banks and trust companies seeking OCC licensing, payment processors, crypto exchanges and custodians

entries.title: CFTC sends its part 4 commodity pool operator and commodity trading advisor information collection to OMB for renewal, comments due December 23, 2026
entries.facts: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission published a notice in the Federal Register of November 23, 2026, document 2026-23801, titled Agency Information Collection Activities Under OMB Review, action line Notice. The collection is titled Rules Relating to the Operations and Activities of Commodity Pool Operators and Commodity Trading Advisors and to Monthly Reporting by Futures Commission Merchants, OMB Control No. 3038-0005. The dates line reads: Comments must be submitted on or before December 23, 2026. The abstract states that the collections of information are required by part 4 of the Commission's regulations, 17 CFR part 4, and that they require commodity pool operators and commodity trading advisors to maintain books and records. The notice states an estimated 49,083 respondents and an estimated total annual burden of 432,325 hours.
entries.source_label: Federal Register document 2026-23801, CFTC, published November 23, 2026, retrieved as the govinfo Federal Register PDF
entries.relevant_to: commodity pool operators, commodity trading advisors, futures commission merchants, digital asset fund managers registered with the CFTC

entries.title: CFTC sends its part 41 security futures products information collection to OMB for renewal, comments due December 23, 2026, affecting two designated contract markets and eight futures commission merchants
entries.facts: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission published a second notice in the Federal Register of November 23, 2026, document 2026-23800, titled Agency Information Collection Activities Under OMB Review, action line Notice. The collection is titled Part 41 Relating to Security Futures Products, OMB Control No. 3038-0059. The Federal Register record gives the comment close date as December 23, 2026. The abstract states that Section 4d(c) of the Commodity Exchange Act, 7 U.S.C. 6d(c), requires the CFTC to consult with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and concerns dually registered firms, security futures products, and segregation versus securities account treatment. The notice states a total of 10 respondents, described as 2 designated contract markets and 8 futures commission merchants, an estimated average burden of 60 hours per respondent and an estimated total annual burden of 603 hours.
entries.source_label: Federal Register document 2026-23800, CFTC, published November 23, 2026, retrieved as the govinfo Federal Register PDF, with the comment close date confirmed against the Federal Register documents API record
entries.relevant_to: designated contract markets, futures commission merchants, dually registered broker-dealers, security futures venues
